newsitem.title: MOROCCO: Morocco's CADEM firm turnover up to $25.1 mln.
newsitem.headline: Morocco's CADEM firm turnover up to $25.1 mln.

text.p: Morocco's cement firm Les Ciments Artificiels de Meknes (CADEM) on Thursday reported a rise of 11.0 percent in turnover to 218.5 million dirhams ($25.1 million) in the first half of the year over the same period in 1995.
The company's turnover in the first half of 1995 was 196 million dirhams ($22.5 million).
One of the 46 listed companies on the Casablanca stock market, CADEM posted a net profit of 18.9 million dirhams in the first half of 1996, down from 28.3 million dirhams in the same period in 1995.
The company, which was established in 1951 in the central region of Meknes, has an average output of 1.2 million tonnes of cement per year.
The main shareholders are the Moroccan conglomerate Societe Nationale d'Investissement and French group Lafarge Coppee.
